title: Lint was never actually run — ruff is not installed, so code_quality's lint term defaulted to neutral 0.5
evidence: `which ruff` -> not found; scorers/code_quality.py:112 returns 0.5 on FileNotFoundError. The recorded code_quality=0.7888888888888889 (scores.json) reconstructs exactly as (0.5 lint + 0.8666666666666667 structure [2 source files x 1/3, +0.2 test-file bonus] + 1.0 stderr)/3, so no lint defect was observed in this code — the term is a missing-toolchain placeholder.
suggestion: Install ruff in the scoring venv so the python lint term is a measurement rather than a constant; until then treat code_quality for python runs as structure-only.

title: create_book dereferences find_book() without a None guard
evidence: app.py:86 `response = jsonify(dict(find_book(book_id)))` — find_book (app.py:69) returns None when the row is absent; a concurrent DELETE between the committed INSERT (app.py:82-85) and this SELECT makes dict(None) raise TypeError and turns a successful create into a 500.
suggestion: Build the response from the values already in hand, or re-select inside the same transaction as the INSERT.

title: Defensive behaviour beyond the spec: 64-bit range guards, strict int typing, and an injection assertion
evidence: app.py:9-10,54-59 reject a `year` outside the signed-64-bit range and reject bool via `type(x) is not int`; app.py:70,111,123 return 404 for path ids above SQLITE_INTEGER_MAX that Flask's `<int:>` converter would otherwise accept; test_app.py:40 asserts `?author=' OR 1=1 --` returns []; test_app.py:73-78 reopens the app against the same file to prove SQLite persistence.
suggestion: None — recorded as an above-spec signal for cross-run comparison, not a deduction.
